title: Seventh Word Satans Deception And The Dialogue Over Talisman Medicine And Ticket

questions.question: What kind of person came to the soldier later in the story, and from which side did he come?
questions.answer: A dishonest and immoral man came from the left side.

questions.question: What things did this man bring to attract the soldier?
questions.answer: He brought fancy decorations, appealing images, imagined pleasures, intoxicating drinks, music, and tasty food.

questions.question: What was the first invitation this man gave the soldier?
questions.answer: He invited him to enjoy himself through drinking, entertainment, and physical pleasures.

questions.question: When the man asked what the soldier was whispering, what was the answer?
questions.answer: The soldier said he was reciting a protective formula.

questions.question: How did the tempter react to the soldier’s recitation?
questions.answer: He mocked it and told him to stop because he thought it would ruin their enjoyment.

questions.question: What did the soldier say he was holding in his hand?
questions.answer: He said he had medicine.

questions.question: Why did the man tell the soldier to throw away the medicine?
questions.answer: He tried to make him think he was fine and should only focus on pleasure.

questions.question: What were the paper with five marks used for?
questions.answer: It served as a travel pass and a provision card.

questions.question: How did the man try to make the soldier reject the paper?
questions.answer: He urged him to tear it up by saying there was no need for a journey during such a pleasant season.

questions.question: Was the soldier fully protected from the man’s tricks at first? Explain.
questions.answer: No. He began to be influenced and almost accepted the deception.

questions.question: What general lesson is stated right after this moment of weakness?
questions.answer: Human beings can be misled by clever deception.

questions.question: What changed the situation suddenly?
questions.answer: A powerful warning voice came from the right.

questions.question: What was the first message of that voice?
questions.answer: It warned the soldier not to be fooled.

questions.question: What challenge was the soldier told to give the trickster about the lion?
questions.answer: He was told to ask whether the man could get rid of the lion behind him.

questions.question: What challenge was given concerning the gallows and the wounds?
questions.answer: He was told to ask whether the man could remove the gallows ahead of him and stop the harms striking him from both sides.

questions.question: What final test did the voice give regarding the journey?
questions.answer: The soldier was told to ask whether the man could cancel the difficult journey ahead.

questions.question: If the man could not do these things, what should happen?
questions.answer: He should stop talking and remain silent.

questions.question: Whose way of speaking was the soldier told to follow?
questions.answer: He was told to speak like the Allah-inspired guide who had helped him earlier.

questions.question: How is the man who approaches the soldier presented in terms of character?
questions.answer: He is shown as crafty, morally corrupt, and dangerous in the way he deceives.

questions.question: What does the man’s offer reveal about his priorities?
questions.answer: He cares about immediate pleasure and distraction, not truth, safety, or the future.

questions.question: Why are decorated objects, images, and intoxicants important in this scene?
questions.answer: They are tools of temptation meant to weaken the soldier’s judgment.

questions.question: What does the soldier’s quiet recitation suggest about his condition?
questions.answer: It suggests he is holding on to spiritual protection.

questions.question: Why does the tempter call the recitation meaningless?
questions.answer: He wants the soldier to stop using what protects him so he can deceive him more easily.

questions.question: How does the man try to redefine the soldier’s situation regarding the medicine?
questions.answer: He falsely claims the soldier is fine and does not need healing.

questions.question: What do the ticket and rations card suggest about the soldier’s future?
questions.answer: They show that he has an important journey ahead and needs preparation.

questions.question: Why does the tempter want those papers destroyed?
questions.answer: He wants the soldier to abandon readiness for what lies ahead.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by saying the soldier was somewhat persuaded?
questions.answer: It teaches that even serious danger does not automatically protect a person from temptation.

questions.question: Why is the statement about human beings being deceived important?
questions.answer: It turns the scene into a lesson about all people, not just one soldier.

questions.question: What is the effect of the voice coming from the right?
questions.answer: It brings clarity, warning, and a way to answer false temptation.

questions.question: Why does the voice tell the soldier to ask the trickster to remove the lion, gallows, wounds, and journey?
questions.answer: It exposes whether the tempter has any real power over the soldier’s actual problems.

questions.question: What contrast is set up between the man from the left and the voice from the right?
questions.answer: One side calls to heedlessness and pleasure, while the other calls to truth, caution, and clear thinking.

questions.question: Why is the command to speak like the earlier guide meaningful?
questions.answer: It tells the soldier to answer deception with the same truth-based wisdom he was already taught.

questions.question: Summarize the main event of the passage in two or three sentences.
questions.answer: A deceptive man comes to the soldier and tries to pull him away from his protective recitation, medicine, and travel documents by offering pleasure and entertainment. The soldier begins to be influenced, but a powerful voice warns him and teaches him how to answer the deceiver.

questions.question: What strategy does the tempter use first: force, fear, or attraction?
questions.answer: He uses attraction.

questions.question: Give two examples of how the tempter tries to appeal to the soldier’s desires.
questions.answer: He offers entertainment and physical pleasure, and he encourages drinking and feasting.

questions.question: What three things does the tempter try to make the soldier abandon?
questions.answer: His spiritual protection, his healing remedy, and his preparation for the journey.

questions.question: What false claim does the tempter make about the soldier’s condition?
questions.answer: He claims the soldier is healthy and has no real problem.

questions.question: What is wrong with the man’s advice about tearing up the travel paper?
questions.answer: It ignores the fact that the journey is still real and preparation is still necessary.

questions.question: How does the passage show that temptation can sound friendly?
questions.answer: The man speaks in a casual, inviting way as if he is offering companionship and fun.

questions.question: What does the soldier’s partial persuasion reveal about human nature?
questions.answer: People can be drawn toward harmful things even when warning signs are present.

questions.question: What tone does the voice from the right use?
questions.answer: It uses a strong, urgent, warning tone.

questions.question: Why are the lion, gallows, wounds, and journey mentioned again by the voice?
questions.answer: They remind the soldier of the serious realities that pleasure cannot remove.

questions.question: What test of truth does the voice teach the soldier to use?
questions.answer: He should ask whether the one making the offer can actually remove the real dangers he faces.

questions.question: According to the voice, what should the soldier do if the trickster cannot solve those problems?
questions.answer: He should reject the invitation and tell the trickster to be silent.

questions.question: What role does memory of earlier guidance play in this passage?
questions.answer: It gives the soldier a model for how to respond when deception appears.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the tempter mainly trying to do to the soldier?
questions.answer: He is trying to turn him away from what protects, heals, and prepares him.

questions.question: What does the tempter’s reaction to the talisman show about his attitude toward spiritual means?
questions.answer: He dismisses them and wants the soldier to see them as useless.

questions.question: How does the tempter speak about the medicine, and what does that reveal?
questions.answer: He tells the soldier to get rid of it, which shows he wants him to neglect his real need.

questions.question: Why might the season being pleasant make the tempter’s argument sound convincing?
questions.answer: A beautiful moment can make a person forget future hardship and become careless.

questions.question: What emotional weakness in the soldier does the passage openly admit?
questions.answer: He was somewhat taken in by the deceptive appeal.

questions.question: What is the significance of the warning voice coming from the opposite side?
questions.answer: It highlights a sharp contrast between misguidance and right guidance.

questions.question: What is the first command the voice gives?
questions.answer: It tells the soldier to stay alert and not be deceived.

questions.question: How does the voice train the soldier to respond intelligently rather than emotionally?
questions.answer: It tells him to challenge the deceiver with concrete questions about real dangers.

questions.question: What do all the voice’s challenges have in common?
questions.answer: They all ask whether the tempter can remove actual threats and suffering.

questions.question: Why is the trickster unable to meet the challenge?
questions.answer: He can offer only temporary amusement, not true rescue.

questions.question: What does the phrase about showing his power really demand from the tempter?
questions.answer: It demands proof, not empty promises.

questions.question: What should happen if proof cannot be given?
questions.answer: The deceiver’s invitation should be rejected.

questions.question: What does the final instruction to speak like the earlier guide suggest about proper speech?
questions.answer: It should be grounded in wisdom, truth, and confidence rather than confusion.

questions.question: Who are the two opposing influences in this passage?
questions.answer: One is the deceptive man who invites the soldier to pleasure, and the other is the strong warning voice that calls him to caution and truth.

questions.question: How does the deceptive man make himself appealing at first?
questions.answer: He surrounds himself with beauty, entertainment, and enjoyment.

questions.question: What does he want the soldier to stop doing with the talisman?
questions.answer: He wants him to stop using it altogether.

questions.question: How does the man describe the talisman, and why is that description misleading?
questions.answer: He treats it as meaningless, but that is misleading because he wants to cut the soldier off from protection.

questions.question: What practical item besides the medicine does the soldier hold?
questions.answer: He holds a document for travel and provisions.

questions.question: Why is that item important within the story?
questions.answer: It shows the soldier is not meant to settle into pleasure because he still must continue a serious journey.

questions.question: In what way does the tempter try to reshape the soldier’s priorities?
questions.answer: He pushes him to prefer present enjoyment over long-term safety and preparation.

questions.question: What warning about people in general is stated directly in the passage?
questions.answer: People are capable of being tricked by clever falsehood.

questions.question: What sound image is used for the voice that comes from the right?
questions.answer: It is described as sounding like thunder.

questions.question: What effect does that sound image create?
questions.answer: It gives a sense of power, urgency, and authority.

questions.question: Why does the voice tell the soldier to confront the trickster with conditions?
questions.answer: So the trickster’s emptiness will become obvious.

questions.question: Name the four conditions the trickster would need to fulfill.
questions.answer: He would need to remove the lion, take away the gallows, stop the harms from both sides, and prevent the journey ahead.

questions.question: What do these conditions prove about the tempter’s promises?
questions.answer: They prove his promises are shallow because they do not address the soldier’s actual situation.

questions.question: What is the right response to someone who cannot remove real danger but only offers distraction?
questions.answer: Their call should be refused.

questions.question: Why is the earlier Allah-inspired guide mentioned again at the end?
questions.answer: He represents the truthful model the soldier should follow when answering deception.

questions.question: What happens first in the passage after some time has passed?
questions.answer: The soldier sees a deceitful man approach him from the left.

questions.question: What signs show that this man is trying to tempt rather than help?
questions.answer: He brings flashy attractions, promotes intoxication and entertainment, and tells the soldier to abandon what benefits him.

questions.question: What does the man invite the soldier to enjoy?
questions.answer: Drinking, amusement, attractive images, music, and food.

questions.question: What is the soldier doing quietly when the man questions him?
questions.answer: He is reciting a protective formula under his breath.

questions.question: How does the man speak about the soldier’s recitation?
questions.answer: He speaks about it with disrespect and treats it like a barrier to fun.

questions.question: What does the soldier identify as medicine?
questions.answer: Something he is carrying in his hand as a remedy.

questions.question: What reasoning does the man use to get rid of the medicine?
questions.answer: He insists there is no illness or problem and says it is a time for enjoyment.

questions.question: What else does the man tell the soldier to destroy?
questions.answer: He tells him to tear up his journey paper and food allowance paper.

questions.question: What mistaken idea lies behind the words about the beautiful spring?
questions.answer: The idea that pleasant surroundings mean there is no need to prepare for what is coming.

questions.question: Did the soldier remain completely firm before the warning voice came?
questions.answer: No, he was partly swayed.

questions.question: What personal reflection is included after that?
questions.answer: A confession that the same kind of deception had also led another person astray.

questions.question: From where does the correcting voice come, and how is it described?
questions.answer: It comes from the right and sounds forceful like thunder.

questions.question: What is the first protective instruction given by the voice?
questions.answer: The soldier is told to be on guard against deception.

questions.question: What is the deeper purpose of asking whether the trickster can remove the lion and gallows?
questions.answer: It shows that real help must deal with life’s serious threats, not merely offer pleasure.

questions.question: What is the soldier told to say if the trickster cannot solve those problems?
questions.answer: He should tell him to stop speaking.

questions.question: Why does the passage end by directing the soldier to speak like the earlier guide?
questions.answer: Because truth should answer falsehood with wisdom learned from sound guidance.
